title: Advanced 3D Liver Models for In vitro Genotoxicity Testing Following Long-Term Nanomaterial Exposure
protocol: Pre-warm DMEM cell culture medium in a 37 °C water bath for 30 min.
Remove one vial of HepG2 cells from liquid nitrogen and thaw in a 37 °C water bath for 2-3 min, gently swirling the vial.
Spray the outer surface of the vial with 70% ethanol to decontaminate before placing under a sterile Class II laminar tissue culture hood.
Pipette the contents of the cryovial into a centrifuge tube containing 9 mL of pre-warmed DMEM cell culture medium (with supplements).
Transfer 10 mL of the cell suspension into a 25 cm² disposable cell culture flask and incubate at 5% CO₂ and 37 °C until ~80% confluency is reached.
Sub-culture cells into a larger 75 cm² disposable cell culture flask.
Sub-culture cells once they reach 80% confluency.
Trypsinize cells with pre-warmed 0.05% trypsin/EDTA solution for 6-8 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Gently tap the flask to dislodge cells from the bottom of the flask.
Add 5 mL of DMEM cell culture medium (with supplements) to neutralize the trypsin enzyme.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Pipette the cell suspension up and down thoroughly to ensure complete dissociation of cells.
Centrifuge the diluted cell suspension at 230 x g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant into disinfectant.
Re-suspend cell pellet in 25 mL of DMEM cell culture medium (with supplements).
Transfer cell suspension into a 75 cm² disposable cell culture flask.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO₂ for 3 days before spheroid preparation.
Determine the cell concentration once cells reach ~80% confluency.
Resuspend the cell-pellet in 1 mL of pre-warmed DMEM culture medium after centrifugation.
Pipette cell suspension up and down thoroughly.
Mix 1 mL of Trypan blue solution with a 1:1 ratio of cell suspension.
Filter 1 mL of Trypan blue solution using a 0.45 µm filter unit into a sterile tube.
Transfer 10 μL of filtered Trypan blue solution into a 0.2 mL tube.
Add 10 μL of cell suspension to the tube containing Trypan blue solution.
Store remaining filtered Trypan blue solution up to 3 months at room temperature for future use.
Spray the haemocytometer thoroughly with 70% ethanol and wipe dry with a sterile paper towel.
Secure the coverslip on top using breath vapor.
Slide the coverslip across the breath moistened surface of the hemocytometer.
Gently pipette the Trypan blue cell suspension up and down using a 1000 μL pipette before adding 10 μL to the haemocytometer.
Ensure that the solution is dispersed underneath the cover slip and covers the entire grid without air bubbles.
Count live (unstained) and dead (stained blue) cells found in the four large corner squares of the haemocytometer under the microscope.
Exclude any cells found to overlap or sit on the interior two edges of the large corner squares from the count.
Prepare a 10 mL stock solution of HepG2 cell suspension in DMEM cell culture medium at a concentration of 2.0 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Mix the cell suspension thoroughly by gently pipetting up and down using a 1000 µL pipette.
Add 100 µL of sterile, room temperature PBS to each well of a 96-well cell culture plate to prevent drying out during incubation.
Invert the lid of a standard flat bottom 96-well cell culture plate and carefully pipette 20 µL drops of the cell suspension into the center of each well groove on the lid.
Center the drops within the grooves of the wells laid out on the lid to ensure they hang in the center when the lid is turned over.
Gently flip the lid of the 96-well plate so that the drops are hanging.
Carefully place the inverted lid with hanging drops onto a 96-well cell culture plate.
Place the entire 96 well plate with lid gently into an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 3 days prior to spheroid transfer onto agarose.
Prepare agarose gels and autoclave prior to the day of plate coating.
Weigh 0.30 g of agarose into a clean, glass bottle.
Add 20 mL of phenol-red free DMEM medium to the agarose.
Autoclave the agarose for 1 h at 230 °C for sterilization.
Coat wells of a 96-well plate with a fine layer of 1.5% agarose gel on day 3 post seeding into hanging drops.
Transfer HepG2 spheroids from hanging drop to agarose-coated wells in 96-well plate on day 3 post seeding.
Remove the 96-well plate containing HepG2 hanging drop spheroids from the incubator.
Flip the lid carefully so that the spheroids are no longer hanging.
Using a multichannel pipette, remove and discard 100 μL of PBS from the base of the 96-well plate.
Allow the plates to air dry for 2-3 minutes while heating the agarose in preparation for coating.
Heat the glass bottle containing 20 mL of pre-prepared 1.5% agarose gel in a microwave at maximum wattage (e.g., 900 W) for 30 seconds.
Gently swirl the melted agarose by rotating the glass bottle to remove any bubbles.
Add 50 μL of agarose into the base of each well of the 96-well plate.
When adding agarose, ensure not to angle the plate >45°.
Allow the plate to stand for 2 min at room temperature.
Add 100 µL of pre-warmed DMEM cell culture medium with supplements on top of the solid agarose layer in each well.
Centrifuge the plate for 3 min at 200 x g to transfer spheroids from hanging droplets into individual wells.
Allow spheroids to settle for 24 h in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Gently aspirate 50 µL of cell culture medium from the surface of each well every 3 days.
Replace with fresh 50 µL of DMEM cell culture medium to refresh the medium.
Disperse the test ENM according to the NanoGenoTox Dispersion Protocol.
Dilute the dispersed ENM suspension from 2.56 mg/mL to the final desired concentration in pre-warmed DMEM cell culture medium.
Aspirate 50 μL of cell culture medium from each well using a 200 µL pipette, leaving 50 µL in the well.
Replace the aspirated volume with 50 μL of medium containing the test toxicant at the required dose.
Incubate the plates for the desired exposure time at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Harvest supernatant from each well in the 96-well plate after the exposure period ends.
Pool and store 50 μL of harvested supernatant at -80°C for further analysis.
Replace cell culture medium in each well with 50 μL of fresh medium containing 6 µg/mL of Cytochalasin B.
Incubate the cells for 1 to 1.5 cell cycles (24 to 26 hours for HepG2).
Remove the 96-well plate from the incubator after exposure treatments.
Using a pipette, aspirate 100 μL of cell culture medium including spheroid tissue from each well.
Collect the aspirated material in a sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Avoid contact with agarose during aspiration.
Centrifuge the spheroid suspension at 230 x g for 5 min.
Remove and store the supernatant at -80 °C.
Re-suspend the pellet in 1 mL of sterile, room temperature PBS (1x).
Centrifuge the spheroid suspension again at 230 x g for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Re-suspend the pellet in 500 µL of 0.05% trypsin-EDTA solution.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 6-8 min.
Gently pipette the trypsinized cells up and down to fully disassociate.
Neutralize with 1 mL of DMEM cell culture medium.
Centrifuge the diluted cell suspension at 230 x g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant into disinfectant.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 2 mL of room temperature PBS (1x).
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 230 x g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant into disinfectant.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 2 mL of cold PBS (1x).
Ensure cells are well dispersed to prevent clumps.
Dip frosted microscope slides in 70% ethanol.
Rinse frosted microscope slides with ddH2O.
Leave frosted microscope slides to air dry for 5 min.
Place prepared microscope slides into cuvette funnel as shown.
Arrange cuvette funnels in the cytocentrifuge with the funnel facing up.
Add 100 μL of cell suspension directly into each cuvette funnel.
Cytospin for 5 min at 500 x g to distribute cells evenly on the slide.
Leave slides to air dry before fixation in ice-cold, 90% methanol for 10 min.
Leave fixed slides to air dry overnight at room temperature.
Store dried slides at -20 °C for up to 6 months.
Remove pre-prepared microscope slides from -20 °C freezer and allow to warm to room temperature before staining.
Prepare a 20% Giemsa staining solution (25 mL) diluted in phosphatase buffer (pH 6.8).
Mix the staining solution thoroughly by gently swirling.
Filter the stained solution using folded filter paper placed in a funnel.
Using a Pasteur pipette, add 3 – 5 drops of filtered Giemsa solution to the cytodot on each slide.
Leave the slides with the Giemsa solution for 8 – 10 minutes.
Wash the slides in two successive phosphatase buffer washes.
Rinse the slides briefly under cold water to remove any excess stain.
Allow the slides to air dry completely.
In a fume hood, dip stained slides in xylene for 10 seconds.
Add a drop of mounting medium to the center of the cytodot on each slide.
Place a glass coverslip over the mounting medium.
Leave the microscope slides in the fume hood overnight to dry before manual scoring.
Based on the proportion of micronuclei present per number of mononucleated or binucleated cells scored, calculate a percentage of genotoxicity value.
Take a measure of cytotoxicity alongside to ensure the DNA damage is not due to cell debris caused by apoptotic cells.
Depending on the presence of Cytochalasin B, use either CPBI or RVCC calculation for cytotoxicity assessment.
